title: Quotient of a power-series ring by part of a parameter system
statement: Let $S$ be either $K[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ for a field $K$, or $\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ for a Cohen ring $\Lambda$ with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], with its maximal ideal and power-series structure [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. If $z_1,\ldots,z_r\in S$ extend to a regular system of parameters of $S$ (a minimal generating set of the maximal ideal of the regular local ring $S$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], and in the Cohen case this system can be chosen to contain $p$ apart from the $z_i$), then $S/(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ is isomorphic as a local ring to a power-series ring in the remaining $n-r$ variables over $K$, respectively over $\Lambda$, with the images of the other chosen parameters as variables. In the Cohen case $p$ retains its role as the coefficient-ring parameter.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NM (lemma-quotient-power-series-ring-over-Cohen), clauses (2) and (4) and their proof

proof.text: (Field case, all parameters.) Let $A=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ and let $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ be a regular system of parameters. The map $\phi:K[[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]]\to A$ sending $Y_i$ to $y_i$ is the substitution homomorphism supplied by the power-series operations [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], both source and target are complete regular local rings and their maximal ideals are generated by the displayed parameters. The classes of the $y_i$ form a basis of $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2$, so the linear part of $\phi$ is an invertible $K$-matrix. Inducting on the degree, an invertible linear part makes substitution bijective on the finite-dimensional spaces of homogeneous terms of each degree: after coefficients below degree $d$ have been chosen, the degree-$d$ error is corrected uniquely because the induced map on degree-$d$ monomials is the $d$th symmetric power of that matrix. Thus $\phi$ induces an isomorphism modulo every power of the maximal ideals. Completeness [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] then identifies $K[[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]]$ with $A$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NM, proof of (1), lines 9754-9759

proof.text: (Field case, a partial parameter system.) If $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ form part of a regular system of parameters of $A$, extend them to $z_1,\ldots,z_r,y_1,\ldots,y_{n-r}$. Applying the preceding full-parameter isomorphism to this $n$-tuple gives $A\cong K[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_r,Y_1,\ldots,Y_{n-r}]]$. The quotient by the ideal generated by the first $r$ parameters is therefore the quotient of this power-series ring by $(Z_1,\ldots,Z_r)$, which is $K[[Y_1,\ldots,Y_{n-r}]]$ by the coefficientwise definition of formal power series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The extension has $r\le n$, and the quotient identification is local because the maximal ideal is the image of the parameter ideal [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NM, proof of (2), lines 9760-9764

proof.text: (Cohen case, all parameters.) Let $B=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ and let $p,y_1,\ldots,y_n$ be a regular system of parameters. The substitution map $\Lambda[[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]]\to B$ sending $Y_i$ to $y_i$ fixes $\Lambda$ and $p$. The same degree-by-degree argument as in the field case, now with the coefficient-ring parameter $p$ included in the filtration, applies: the classes of $p,y_1,\ldots,y_n$ and of $p,X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are bases of the respective cotangent spaces, so the induced linear map is invertible and its symmetric powers give bijections modulo every maximal-ideal power. Both rings are complete regular local rings by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], hence the substitution map is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NM, proof of (3), line 9765

proof.text: (Cohen case, a partial parameter system.) If $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ together with $p$ form part of a regular system of parameters of $B$, extend them to $p,z_1,\ldots,z_r,y_1,\ldots,y_{n-r}$. The Cohen full-parameter isomorphism gives $B\cong\Lambda[[Z_1,\ldots,Z_r,Y_1,\ldots,Y_{n-r}]]$ over $\Lambda$, with $p$ unchanged. Quotienting by $(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ sets the first variables to zero and leaves $\Lambda[[Y_1,\ldots,Y_{n-r}]]$ by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The parameter count gives $r\le n$; the quotient is local and $p$ remains the coefficient-ring parameter by the maximal-ideal description in [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete].
